class.name: NetwClockHandle
class.brief_description: The tick every peer in the session counts, reached by [method Netw.clock].
class.description:
A tick is a numbered step of the simulation. Every peer counts the same ticks, and a client keeps its count aligned with the server's by measuring the round trip and correcting for it. [member tick] is the number every [NetwRecord] and every lag-compensation query is stamped against. [codeblock] var c := Netw.clock(self) c.before_tick.connect(sample_input) c.on_tick.connect(step) label.text = "tick %d" % c.tick [/codeblock]
[b]How a tick is produced[/b] The clock does not use a timer. It banks the time each physics frame delivers and spends it one tick at a time, so a slow frame produces two ticks and a fast one produces none. [codeblock lang=text] ticktime = 1 / tickrate
# each physics frame, given that frame's delta in seconds accumulator += delta while accumulator >= ticktime accumulator -= ticktime announce a tick, tick += 1 [/codeblock] At a tickrate of 30 under 60 Hz physics the loop announces a tick every second frame. [member physics_factor] is that ratio, 2.0 here, and [member tick_phase] is how far into the current tick the accumulator sits. The loop announces at most [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME] ticks in one frame. A peer that keeps hitting the ceiling cannot catch up, and [member behind_count] is how often that happened.
[b]How a client agrees with the server[/b] The client pings the server every [member ping_interval] seconds and the server answers with its own tick and phase. The answer is already stale by the time it lands, so the client aims ahead of it by the time the trip took. [codeblock lang=text] rtt the round trip this ping and its pong measured, in seconds rtt_avg the mean of the last jitter_window samples jitter the mean distance of those samples from rtt_avg one_way rtt_avg / 2
target = server_tick + server_phase + one_way / ticktime + lead_ticks [/codeblock]
[code]target[/code] is a fractional tick, not a whole one. Keeping the server's phase is what stops the target jumping a full tick each time a pong lands on the other side of a tick boundary. The first pong sets the clock to the target outright, because there is nothing to drift from yet. Every pong after that is handled by [member sync_mode].
[b]Snap and stretch[/b] [constant NetwMultiplayer.SYNC_MODE_SNAP] writes the target straight into the tick and the accumulator. It is correct immediately and it can move the tick backwards, which any code holding a tick number will see. [constant NetwMultiplayer.SYNC_MODE_STRETCH] is the default. It keeps the target as an estimate that advances on its own, then closes a fixed fraction of the remaining gap each frame. [codeblock lang=text] each physics frame estimate += delta * tickrate current = tick + accumulator / ticktime gap = estimate - current accumulator += gap * ticktime * stretch_nudge_factor [/codeblock]
[constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_STRETCH_NUDGE_FACTOR] is that fraction. At 0.05 the clock closes a twentieth of the gap per frame, so it runs slightly fast or slightly slow until the gap is spent and the tick never jumps. Above [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_PANIC_SNAP_THRESHOLD] ticks of gap it snaps instead, because a gap that large is a desync and not drift.
[b]Reading remote state[/b] A remote peer's state is always at least one-way latency old, so the newest tick has nothing in it yet for anyone but this peer. [member display_offset] is how many ticks back the view reads, and the useful value is the one that covers the trip plus the spread in it. [codeblock lang=text] recommended_display_offset = ceil((one_way + jitter * jitter_multiplier) * tickrate) [/codeblock]
Nothing applies that number on its own. [member recommended_display_offset] is the measurement and [member display_offset] is what the clock uses, and [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_auto_configure_offset] is what samples the first for a while and writes the largest reading into the second.

method.name: monitor
method.description: One link or cadence measurement as a [float]. The vocabulary is [enum NetwMultiplayer.ClockMonitor], and every member of it is a uniform scalar so a debug overlay can sample the whole family in a loop. [codeblock] var rtt := Netw.clock(self).monitor(NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_MONITOR_RTT_AVG) [/codeblock] The numbers that shape the simulation are properties. [member physics_factor], [member tick_factor], [member tick_phase] and [member recommended_display_offset] are each read directly.

members.member: How many frames wanted a tick the per-frame ceiling refused. Sustained growth means this peer cannot sustain its own tickrate, which no setting repairs. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_simulation_behind_count].
How many ticks behind [member tick] the view of remote state reads, so that what it reads has already arrived. [member recommended_display_offset] is what the measured link suggests for it.
Whether a [NetwClockConfig] has settled on this session, which is what [method Netw.configure_clock] declares. A component that steps on the tick reads this before it trusts [member tick].
Whether this peer's tick agrees with the server. Always [code]true[/code] on the server, and [code]false[/code] on a client until the first pong lands. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_is_synchronized].
Physics frames per tick, unrounded. A per-frame quantity such as a velocity is scaled by this to cover one tick's worth of ground. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_physics_factor].
How many seconds pass between the pings a client measures the link with. Shorter samples the link more often and costs more packets.
The display offset the measured link suggests, in ticks. Nothing applies it. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_recommended_display_offset].
How a calibration is taken, either [constant NetwMultiplayer.SYNC_MODE_SNAP] at once or [constant NetwMultiplayer.SYNC_MODE_STRETCH] spread over frames.
The current network tick, the number every [NetwRecord] and every lag-compensation query is stamped against. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_tick].

How far the simulation has advanced past the last tick, in ticks, counting the part of the current frame already drawn. This is what a renderer interpolates with. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_tick_factor].
Where the accumulator sits inside the current tick, from zero to one. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_get_tick_phase].
Ticks per second, which [method Netw.configure_clock] declares and nothing changes afterwards. Every peer in a session counts at this rate.

signal.name: before_tick
signal.description: Emitted before the simulation steps [param tick], carrying that step's [param delta]. This is where input for the tick is sampled, because what is written here is what the tick then simulates. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.clock_before_tick].

signal.name: on_tick
signal.description: Emitted as the simulation steps [param tick], carrying that step's [param delta]. Relayed from [signal NetwMultiplayer.clock_on_tick].
